svg.aria-label: Wireframe chapter 4 (desktop 1280px): In the month Australia locked down, crash admissions fell by a third. Cyclist admissions rose.
svg.title: Wireframe chapter 4 (desktop 1280px): In the month Australia locked down, crash admissions fell by a third. Cyclist admissions rose.

g.text: down, crash admissions fell by a
In 2020 Australians travelled less, worked from home and bought
bikes. Hospital records show how that played out on the roads.
April 2020 had 2,357 road-crash admissions, 32% fewer than April 2019 and the lowest
In that month admissions fell for every main road user except cyclists, which rose
From April to December 2020, cyclist admissions beat every same month of the previous
April 2020: a third fewer crash admissions
Notes: Grey band = range of 2015-2019. Lockdown dates and length differed by state (Victoria's was longest); national monthly data can't be split by state.
Every road user went to hospital less in April 2020, except cyclists
Notes: April 2020 vs April 2019, % change by road user. Source: BITRE hospitalised injury data.
Cyclist injuries were already rising. 2020 added to it.
Notes: The trend assumes the 2011-2019 yearly growth rate (about 3.9% a year) simply continued. It is a rough yardstick with no error margin attached.
Restrictions differed by state. Victoria had the largest rise in cyclist admissions in July-
December 2020: 1,419 against 1,010 in 2019 (+40.5%). That fits the timing of its second
lockdown, but six-monthly state data cannot show cause and effect.
Victoria had the largest rise in cyclist admissions in July-December
Notes: Working note: state counts exclude deaths, as in the BITRE state file. Six-monthly data cannot show cause and effect.
